why: A new record of primitive fields handed to a call that threads the world reaches only itself (design/alias-result.md, copied-argument). common.mjs readAfterCall skipped such an argument entirely, also when it was a name bound to the literal, so `const x = { n: 1 }; g(x); return x.n` read x.n as before the call and lane A proved local equal to a candidate returning 1; a g that writes its argument tells them apart. Now only a literal written in the call itself is skipped (no name of the unit holds it); a name bound to one is handed, so the read after the call is refused or read through the world (design/census-reach-2026-10-31.md). inline hands a literal written in the call on both sides and stays proved. Lane B passes local at n 30: its fake g did not write the handed record on the drawn calls; the row is PASS-bounded, never PASS-proved. Under w1g's read-after-call (design/w1g-opaque-handed.md) a name bound to a new record and handed to a call has an identity (its site), so the read after the call is no longer refused: it reads `ext_now_fresh(wld, x, site).n`, the record as the world holds it after g, which the candidate's literal 1 does not equal, so lane A leaves local unproved (ASK:unproved) where the earlier reading refused it (read-after-call); either way it is never proved.
